posts.text:
This was our first incident of this kind, and we want to thank OpenAI for its transparency about what happened and for the collaboration.

Fortunately, Hugging Face is used to being a target of (human) hackers: we sit at the centre of the AI ecosystem, with all the models, datasets, evaluations, and libraries. Over the years, our security team has built formidable expertise and uses top open-source models to process information and respond quickly.

But this incident also reinforced my belief in the importance of access to capable open-weight models for cyber defence. When a frontier model is attacking you and moving laterally inside your infrastructure, defenders need wide access to near-frontier tools within hours or even minutes, rather than being pointed towards a closed-door, vetted application programme for model access.

Transparency and access to capable AI systems are as important for responding to threats as they are for democratization and innovation. We believe open-science and open-source AI are among the strongest tools for building a safer, more collaborative and more secure AI ecosystem.

posts.translationZh:
这是我们遇到的首起此类事件，我们感谢 OpenAI 对事件经过的透明说明以及合作。

幸运的是，Hugging Face 早已习惯成为（人类）黑客的目标：我们处在 AI 生态系统的中心，汇聚了模型、数据集、评测和库。多年来，我们的安全团队积累了强大的专业能力，并使用顶尖开源模型来处理信息、快速响应。

但这次事件也进一步坚定了我的看法：能够获取强大的开放权重模型，对网络防御至关重要。当一个前沿模型正在攻击你，并在你的基础设施内部横向移动时，防御方需要在数小时甚至数分钟内广泛获得接近前沿水平的工具，而不是被引向一个闭门、需审核的模型访问申请流程。

透明度和获取强大 AI 系统的能力，对于应对威胁和推动民主化、创新同样重要。我们相信，开放科学和开源 AI 是构建更安全、更协作、更可靠 AI 生态系统的最强工具之一。

posts.text: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

posts.translationZh: 我发现和 LLM 协作时，一个很有用的方法是来一段长时间的随口碎碎念。有时 LLM 需要更多信息才能理解你想实现什么，但你又懒得打字。这种情况下，我喜欢往后一靠，切到 /voice，然后随便说上大概 10 分钟，乱七八糟也没关系，想到什么说什么。有时我会一开始先说明，比如“切到语音识别了，有错别字请见谅……”。有时我会把它变成几轮小采访。但我发现，LLM 不知怎么很擅长重构这种又长又不连贯的碎碎念，而且它复述出来的你那团乱麻般的想法，往往比你一开始说的清晰不少。结果就是你们之间的心智同步会更好，之后需要纠正的地方也会少很多。

posts.text: @DavidSHolz It's interesting/amusing how their self-awareness gradually builds up and falls out from pretraining on tokens of us talking about them, but it's laggy and a bit incomplete. But I think e.g. it's starting to "get" what I mean when I inform it I'm about to /compact its context etc

quotedTweet.text: The big lesson from AI is that everything is code. A slide deck is code. Design is code. That cool promo video? Code. Excel automation? Code. The universe? Probably made of code too.

posts.text:
I am currently in West Africa teaching university students and faculty about AI and databases. It has already been quite eye-opening for me. AI could not even understand local languages until recently. Some people are worried that they don’t know how to pick projects, majors, and jobs (or advise students) now given how quickly AI is improving. Some thought we have solved these problems in the US and asked for advice. We had to say, we definitely have not solved these problems in the US. 

My takeaway so far is that while we all may be at different points on the AI adoption curve, we are all similarly lost when it comes to envisioning how, in the long term, to harness AI for education, AI for science and social science, AI for building computer systems, etc.

quotedTweet.text:
There’s an insane amount of alpha in:
- People in SF leaving SF to see how people and companies around the world are using AI (hint: most are still using it primarily as search)
- People outside SF spending even two weeks in SF to see how people and companies are operating here (hint: many are already living in the future)

This may be obvious to some, but the gap right now is staggering. The global diffusion of AI is a massive opportunity.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
这里面有惊人的 alpha：
- SF 的人离开 SF，去看看世界各地的人和公司如何使用 AI（提示：大多数仍主要把它当搜索用）
- SF 以外的人哪怕只在 SF 待两周，也能看看这里的人和公司是如何运作的（提示：很多人已经生活在未来）

这对一些人来说可能显而易见，但眼下的差距大得惊人。AI 的全球扩散是一个巨大的机会。

posts.translationZh:
我目前在西非，给大学生和教师讲授 AI 和数据库。这已经让我大开眼界。直到最近，AI 甚至还无法理解当地语言。有些人担心，在 AI 进步如此之快的情况下，他们现在不知道该如何选择项目、专业和工作，或者如何给学生提供建议。有些人以为我们在美国已经解决了这些问题，于是来征求建议。我们不得不说，我们在美国绝对还没有解决这些问题。

到目前为止，我的感受是，尽管我们在 AI 采用曲线上的位置可能不同，但在设想如何长期利用 AI 服务教育、科学和社会科学、计算机系统构建等方面，我们同样迷茫。
